::: {.lead}
Today you make the talk of your course project and present it. There are
no new ideas: you use what you learned in Lectures 6–26. **Part A** is your own talk in
PowerPoint on the lab computer; **Part B** is on a simulator of the
interactive page: on paper, scan its QR code; on the screen, click its
link. After each step, write your result in its box.
:::

## Before you start

- **You need:** a lab computer with PowerPoint (the desktop app works best
  for Presenter View), your files `project.xlsx` and `report.docx` from
  Lecture 28, and an AI assistant that the university allows (for example
  `copilot.microsoft.com`).
- **No lab computer today?** Do Part B of each experiment on your phone. Do
  Part A later on any computer with PowerPoint.
- **Check:** the results are at the end of this worksheet. Look only after
  you try. On the interactive page, every step has a check that answers at
  once.

## Experiment 1 · Five slides and four checks

**The idea (Lectures 17, 21 and 25):** a short talk has five slides: the
title, the question, the chart, the insights and the end. Make them fast
from the Heading 1 titles of your report (**Home › New Slide › Slides from
Outline**) or from an AI outline. Then check every slide four times:
**accuracy** (the numbers are as in Excel), **claims** (the data shows
each sentence), **pictures** (they fit the topic and are fair) and
**honesty** (the end says where AI helped).

**Aim:** make the five slides of your talk, and check them.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In the app (PowerPoint)**
:::

1. Make `talk.pptx` with five slides from your report. Paste your chart
   from Excel on slide 3, and write two insights with numbers from your
   PivotTable on slide 4.

   {{< record "My five slide titles" lines=2 >}}

   ::: {.check}
   Five slides: 1 the title and your name; 2 your question; 3 your chart;
   4 two insights with numbers from your PivotTable; 5 the end: your main
   insight, thanks, and where AI helped.
   :::

   ::: {.order}
   Put the five slides of the project talk in order.

   1. the title and your name
   2. your question
   3. your chart
   4. two insights with numbers
   5. the end: the main insight and the AI use

   Why: The class hears the question first, then sees the answer.
   :::

2. Check your five slides with the four checks, and fix every problem.

   {{< record "The problems that I fixed …" lines=2 >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **Accuracy:** every number as in Excel. **Claims:** the data shows each
   sentence. **Pictures:** they fit the topic and are fair. **Honesty:**
   the last slide says where AI helped. Fix every problem before you
   present.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   Slide 4 says "I studied English 320 minutes", and your PivotTable says
   230 minutes. Which check fails?

   - [x] accuracy

     Why: The number on the slide is not the number in Excel.

   - [ ] claims

     Why: The sentence is about the data; its number is wrong.

   - [ ] honesty

     Why: Honesty is about the AI use.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On the simulator** (no computer? do it on your phone)
:::

{{< sim file="../../week-15/sims/deck-checker.html" poster="../../week-15/sims/deck-checker.png" title="Deck Checker: ready to present?" >}}

3. In **Deck Checker**, mark each of Sami's five slides: OK, or its
   problem. Which check fails on slide 4?

   {{< record "Slide 2 … ; slide 4 … ; slide 5 …" lines=2 >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **Claims** on slide 4: "Everyone loves juice" is not in the data.
   Slide 2: the picture does not fit; slide 3: a wrong number; slide 5:
   no AI-use line. Slide 1 is OK.
   :::

   ::: {.sort}
   Which check fails on each of Sami's slides? Sort them.

   Pictures
   :   slide 2: a big restaurant, for a small canteen

       Why: The picture does not fit the topic.

   Accuracy
   :   slide 3: a total that is not the number in Excel

       Why: Every number is as in Excel.

   Claims
   :   slide 4: "Everyone loves juice"

       Why: The data does not show it.

   Honesty
   :   slide 5: no AI-use line

       Why: The end says where AI helped.
   :::

## Experiment 2 · Rehearse and present

**The idea (Lectures 17 and 18):** a talk of three minutes gives each of
the five slides about 30–40 seconds. Write short speaker notes, not a text
to read. Rehearse once with **Presenter View** and its timer (**Alt +
F5**). Then look at the class, speak slowly, and end with your main
insight.

**Aim:** rehearse your talk, and present it.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In the app (PowerPoint)**
:::

1. Write a short speaker note on each of your five slides (**View ›
   Notes**): a few words to remind you, not a text to read.

   {{< record "My note for slide 3" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   A good note is a short reminder in your own words, for example
   "English takes the most time. Point at the chart." The class reads the
   slide; you say more than it shows.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   Which speaker note is good?

   - [x] English: the most minutes. Point at the chart.

     Why: A short reminder, not a text to read: you look at the class.

   - [ ] a full paragraph that you read aloud, word by word

     Why: Notes are short reminders; reading a text loses the class.

   - [ ] no notes: read the slides aloud

     Why: The class can read the slides: say more than they show.
   :::

2. Rehearse your talk alone with Presenter View and its timer, and write
   the time. If it is too long, cut one sentence on each slide. Present it
   when the teacher calls you.

   {{< record "My time … ; what I cut …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   About three minutes: 30–40 seconds for each slide. Too long? Cut one
   sentence on each slide, and keep the chart and the numbers.
   :::

   ::: {.fill answer="35" tol="5" unit="s" hint="Three minutes are 180 seconds, for five slides."}
   A talk of three minutes has five slides. About how many seconds is each
   slide?

   Why: 180 ÷ 5 = 36 seconds: about 30–40 seconds for each slide.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On the simulator** (no computer? do it on your phone)
:::

{{< sim file="../../week-10/sims/rehearsal-lab.html" poster="../../week-10/sims/rehearsal-lab.png" title="Rehearsal Lab: Presenter View and the timer" >}}

3. In **Rehearsal Lab**, rehearse Sami's talk once, with each slide close
   to its plan. What does the list show, and what is the total?

   {{< record "The list … ; the total …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **"About right"** for every slide, and about **3:00** in all.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   Your rehearsal takes 4:10. What do you cut?

   - [x] one sentence on each slide

     Why: The talk gets shorter, and the chart and the numbers stay.

   - [ ] the chart on slide 3

     Why: The chart and the numbers are the evidence of your talk.

   - [ ] the last slide

     Why: The end says your main insight and where AI helped.
   :::
